newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RAM resigns as Rural Property Trust manager.
newsitem.headline: RAM resigns as Rural Property Trust manager.

text.p: London-based Bankers Trust International Plc (BTI) said on Tuesday its proposal to remove Rural and Agricultural Management (RAM) as manager of Australia's Rural Property Trust (RPT) had succeeded.
RAM had elected to resign just before an extraordinary meeting held on Tuesday, paving the way for appointment of a new management team and corporatisation of the trust, BTI said.

"This is a major victory for all RPT unit holders... Their mandate allowed us to push ahead strongly with our initiatives, which we believe are crucial to the future performance of the trust," BTI managing director Lawrence Hudson said.

BTI, which holds a 19.6 percent stake in RPT, in March requisitioned the extraordinary meeting of unitholders to depose RAM as manager, saying that RAM had "demonstrated a poor track record of profitability".
BTI said RAM had accepted a retirement payout of A$500,000 instead of the A$2.25 million it had sought.
Under the agreement, a five person board will be formed to manage RPT, comprising an independent chairman and one director nominated by each of the four major unit holders.
RAM will retain one seat on the RPT board and all litigation between the parties will be dropped, BT said.
More than 99 percent of the 80 percent of the unitholders who voted supported the agreement, BTI said.
"Under the new structure RPT will, we believe, be well placed to become a substantial and successful player in Australian agriculture," Hudson said in a statement.
Trading in RPT units was suspended by the Australian Stock Exchange on Tuesday pending the outcome of the meeting.
RPT units closed unchanged at A$0.415 on Monday.
